reason: Under Amazon RDS Extended Support charges, the quote states RDS Extended Support charges apply to standby instances in Multi-AZ deployments.
The quote states charges are incurred for all engines enrolled in RDS Extended Support beginning the day after the RDS end of standard support date.
On the RDS Extended Support page, the quote states this paid offering gives you more time to upgrade to a supported major engine version.

The quotes support automatic enrollment on February 29, 2024 and charges starting March 1, 2024, but the claim that February 29, 2024 was the end of standard support date (value eoss) is only in an unquoted context sentence, not in the quotes.

The quotes state charges can be avoided by changing enrollment of a DB instance or cluster via the EngineLifecycleSupport parameter with the CLI or API, and disabling enrollment when already past standard support triggers an automatic upgrade to the next supported major version.

The pricing page quotes state that for provisioned instances on Aurora, RDS for MySQL and RDS for PostgreSQL, Extended Support is priced per vCPU per hour and pricing also depends on the calendar date.

The quotes state Extended Support is available for up to 3 years past the end of standard support for a major engine version, after which RDS automatically upgrades the major engine version if you have not.
The quote states RDS Extended Support allows you to continue running a database on a major engine version past the RDS end of standard support date for an additional cost.
The quote states replication can be set up between an RDS for MySQL or MariaDB DB instance and a MySQL or MariaDB instance external to Amazon RDS using binary log file replication.

Under Failover, the quote states that without RDS Proxy a failover involves a brief outage, writes are not possible, and existing connections are disrupted so the application must reopen them; context scopes failover to Multi-AZ RDS DB instances.

The quote states instance class or allocated storage changes are applied in the maintenance window, or immediately with the apply-immediately flag, which also applies any other pending system changes.
The quote states that when a new minor version contains significant bug fixes, RDS schedules automatic upgrades for DB instances with Auto Minor Version Upgrade set to Yes.
The quote states automated backups enable point-in-time recovery, with a full daily snapshot during the preferred backup window and transaction logs captured as updates are made.
Under the heading asking whether backups must be enabled, the quote states that by default Amazon RDS enables automated backups of your DB instance with a 7-day retention period.

The quotes state AWS Config continuously records configuration changes to RDS DB instances, DB subnet groups, DB snapshots, DB security groups and event subscriptions, and AWS Config Rules can evaluate them.
The quotes state backup size is directly proportional to the data on the instance and subsequent backups are incremental, storing only changed data.
The quote states Amazon RDS can automatically back up your database and keep your database software up to date with the latest version.

The quote states storage I/O may be briefly suspended during backup initialization (typically under a few seconds), and there is no I/O suspension for Multi-AZ DB deployments since the backup is taken from the standby.
The quote states Amazon RDS DB snapshots and automated backups are stored in S3.
The quote states instance hours are billed for each hour the instance is running in an available state and you must stop or delete it to avoid additional instance hours.
The quote states partial instance hours are billed in one-second increments with a 10 minute minimum charge after a billable status change such as creating, starting or modifying the instance class.
The billing list item states Provisioned IOPS per month is billed at the provisioned IOPS rate regardless of IOPS consumed, for Provisioned IOPS (SSD) storage only.
The quote states a stopped instance is charged for provisioned storage (including Provisioned IOPS) and backup storage but not for DB instance hours.
The quote lists exactly Aurora MySQL, Aurora PostgreSQL, RDS for MySQL, RDS for MariaDB and RDS for PostgreSQL as engines with Blue/Green Deployments.
The quote states the blue environment is the current production environment and the green environment is the staging environment that becomes production after switchover.
Under switchover guardrails, the quote states you can specify maximum tolerable downtime as low as 30 seconds and an ongoing transaction exceeding it makes the switchover time out.
The quotes state Blue/Green Deployments do not delete the old production environment and standard billing applies to old production instances until you delete them.

The quotes support blocking writes on both environments until switchover completes, green catching up, and writes enabled on green afterwards with zero data loss as the design goal, but redirecting traffic to green is only in an unquoted context sentence, and the claim drops the quote's 'designed to' hedge.
The quotes list major or minor engine upgrades, OS updates, schema changes that do not break logical replication and parameter changes as ideal use cases, achieved with short, predictable downtime.

Under the heading asking for a history of all RDS API calls (answered Yes), the quote states CloudTrail records API calls for your account, enabling security analysis, resource change tracking and compliance auditing.
The quote states the database is temporarily unavailable while the instance class is modified, typically a few minutes, during the maintenance window unless applied immediately.
The quote states Database Savings Plans can be purchased for RDS usage and reduce costs by up to 35% with a commitment to consistent usage over a 1-year term.
The quotes state a final DB snapshot can be created on deletion and used to restore later, and RDS retains it along with all other manual snapshots after deletion.
The quotes state that selecting Connect to an EC2 compute resource on Create database makes RDS automate networking setup such as security groups, subnets and ingress/egress rules (also a VPC).
The quote states encryption is added to an unencrypted instance by creating a snapshot, copying it with a KMS key, and restoring an encrypted instance from the encrypted snapshot.
The quote states Amazon RDS supports encryption at rest for all database engines using keys managed with AWS KMS.
The quote states that on an encrypted instance the data at rest in underlying storage is encrypted, as are its automated backups, read replicas and snapshots.
The quote names RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle and Db2 as the familiar engines Amazon RDS gives access to.
The quote, referring to Enhanced Monitoring named in the preceding sentence, states it is enabled per instance with a chosen granularity all the way down to 1 second.
The quote states Enhanced Monitoring supports all Amazon RDS database engines.
